framework: Bank of England PRA SS1/23 — model risk management

articles.title: Model inventory: a complete record of models in use, with ownership
articles.note: The registry is the inventory. This checks each entry is attributable and tiered; whether the inventory is complete cannot be checked from inside — a model nobody registered is invisible here by construction. An inventory that cannot name the model is a list of participants, so every active AGENT must declare a model id; TOOL, SYSTEM, HUMAN and VALIDATOR participants are not asked, because they run no model and a finding nobody can act on is how a report stops being read. A deployment with no registered agents reports UNKNOWN rather than satisfied: an inventory of nothing is an answer to a different question.

articles.title: Model risk tiering proportionate to materiality
articles.note: Checks a tier is declared, not that it is the right tier. Whether a tier matches the materiality of what the model does is a judgement this cannot make.

articles.title: Controls: limits on model output, with human review where appropriate
articles.note: The gate policy is the control. This checks the controls exist and are not self-approvable; whether they are set at the right thresholds is a judgement for the second line. Limits are also read directly from the registry: an irreversible action that declares no cap on magnitude or rate is reported, because P4.3 asks for limits on output and an unbounded irreversible action has none. `Manifest.validate` accepts such an action — it checks a limits block only if one is present — so this is a real gap rather than a restatement of what admission already refuses. What is checked is that a limit is declared, not that the number is the right number, which is a judgement about the business and not a property of this registry.
